rows.name: coin_count_display
rows.notes: HUD coin count ("x NN"), two BCD digits: 0x07ED = tens, 0x07EE = ones. Distinct from the binary 1-UP counter 0x075E. Differential search (no reference): one ? block coin made 0x075E go 1->2 while the visible count 56->57; the two-digit value "57" read back as [5,7] at 0x07ED/0x07EE, matching the HUD. Proof by write: while paused I wrote 0x07ED=4, 0x07EE=2 (display value 42) and 0x075E=42, then collected a coin; the HUD coin field redrew as "x43" and RAM read [4,3].

rows.name: level_timer
rows.notes: HUD TIME countdown, three BCD digits: 0x07F8 = hundreds, 0x07F9 = tens, 0x07FA = ones (starts at 400). Differential search (no reference): with Mario standing still, snapshot->200 frames of empty input->snapshot and filter 'decreased' left 10 survivors including 0x07F8 (3->2) and 0x07FA (8->3); the tens digit only fell on a borrow, and a second window dropped 0x07FA because the ones digit wraps UP on borrow. Proof by write: wrote [1,2,3] then [3,0,0] then [3,9,9] to 0x07F8-0x07FA while paused; the HUD redrew as 106/292/391 respectively and RAM matched, i.e. the game keeps counting down from the written value.

rows.name: player_score
rows.notes: HUD MARIO score, six BCD digits, most significant first: 0x07DD (10^6) 0x07DE (10^5) 0x07DF (10^4) 0x07E0 (10^3) 0x07E1 (10^2) 0x07E2 (10^1). The ones place is NOT stored - the HUD draws a fixed trailing "0". Differential search (no reference): collecting a ? block coin added 200 and moved the 10^2 digit (0x07E1 7->9) plus carry into 10^3. Extent proven by writing six distinct digits [9,8,7,6,5,4] to 0x07DD-0x07E2 while paused: all six appeared ("9876540"), and after the coin that followed, the HUD read "9876740" (my 9876540 + 200) with RAM [9,8,7,6,7,4].
